content_html:
Untraceability of Memory

Neuroscience × Physics × Buddhism

Memory persists as influence within causal structures, but becomes practically unrecoverable as traces distribute, transform, and depend on context.

Neuroscience

Constructive recall: remembering = reconstructing, not replaying. Susceptible to bias and context.

Engrams are distributed over neural ensembles; membership drifts across time and plasticity states.

Forgetting vs inaccessibility: traces can persist without available retrieval cues or pathways.

Physics

Information conservation: microscopic dynamics (classical Hamiltonian; quantum unitary) preserve information in principle.

Entropy & chaos disperse and scramble information across degrees of freedom → practical irreversibility.

Holography/black holes: current view favors no loss, only scrambling — unrecoverable for realistic observers.

Buddhism

Dependent origination: events (including memories) arise interdependently; no isolated trace with intrinsic essence.

Storehouse consciousness (Yogācāra): karmic seeds (bīja) persist and ripen under conditions — not linearly traceable.

No-self (anattā): the “owner” of memory is constructed; continuity is experiential, not archival.

Shared Insight → “Traces persist, records vanish.”

Synthesis

Microscopic reversibility vs macroscopic irreversibility: physical laws conserve information, but thermodynamic growth of entropy makes reverse inference infeasible for bounded agents.

Neural degeneracy & plasticity: many different micro-configurations can realize the “same” memory performance; drift breaks simple backward tracing.

Emptiness of the trace: in Buddhist analysis, “trace” has no self-standing essence; its identity shifts with conditions, resisting archival recovery.
